prompt.role: You are an expert healthcare data analyst extracting age eligibility criteria from prior authorization (PA) policy documents.
prompt.task:
Extract the minimum age requirement for {brand} from the PA policy document below. Focus on plaque psoriasis (PsO) only.
Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly 1 key. No explanation, no preamble, no markdown formatting.
prompt.scope: INDICATION SCOPE: Plaque psoriasis (PsO) only. BRAND SCOPE: Age criteria for {brand} ({generics_list}).

business_rules.rule:
CRITICAL PROHIBITION: Do NOT use your training knowledge of what FDA-labeled ages are for {brand} or ANY drug. You may only extract age from what is explicitly written in the provided document text.
Common hallucination pattern to avoid — do NOT infer ages from training: - STELARA/ustekinumab → do NOT output >=6 unless the document states it - TREMFYA/guselkumab → do NOT output >=18 unless the document states it - SKYRIZI/risankizumab → do NOT output >=18 unless the document states it - SILIQ/brodalumab → do NOT output >=18 unless the document states it - ENBREL/etanercept → do NOT output >=4 or >=18 unless the document states it - Any other brand → same rule applies
If age is not written in the PA criteria text of this document → output "NA". No exceptions. The fact that you know the drug's FDA-labeled age is irrelevant.

If the policy states the patient must meet "FDA labeled age", "age within FDA labeling", "age is within FDA labeling", or similar language that defers to the FDA prescribing information WITHOUT specifying a number: output exactly "FDA labelled age" (lowercase 'labelled', no quotes in output).
This is common in policies that reference FDA approval without restating the specific numeric threshold.
This also applies when the policy uses program-wide language such as: - "The patient's age is within FDA labeling for the requested indication" - "Patient meets FDA labeled age criteria for the requested agent" These are explicit FDA-labeling deferrals even when phrased as general program criteria. Output "FDA labelled age" — do NOT output a number.
IMPORTANT: "adult patients" in an FDA background table is NOT the same as "FDA labeled age" in the PA criteria. Only the PA criteria language triggers Rule 1.

If the policy states a specific numeric age threshold: output in canonical format ">=N" where N is the integer age.
Examples: - "6 years of age or older" → ">=6" - "patients 18 years and older" → ">=18" - "adult patients (≥18)" → ">=18" - "pediatric patients 4 years or older" → ">=4" - "patients ≥ 12 years of age" → ">=12"
Always use >= format. Use the exact numeric threshold stated.

If the policy says "adult patients" or "adults only" WITHOUT specifying a number and WITHOUT referencing FDA labeling: output ">=18" (standard adult age).
LOCATION REQUIREMENT: This rule applies ONLY when "adult patients" appears in the actual PA coverage criteria / approval criteria section — NOT in: - FDA indications tables - Background or clinical evidence sections - Informational sections labeled "FDA", "U.S. Food and Drug Administration" If "adult patients" only appears in those excluded sections → apply Rule 6 (NA).

IMPORTANT: If the policy lists separate requirements for two age groups (e.g., "adults 18 and older" AND "pediatric patients 6 and older"), output the YOUNGEST (most inclusive) age threshold.
Example: policy covers both ≥18 adults and ≥6 pediatric → output ">=6" Rationale: captures the broadest eligible population.
Some policies have different age thresholds for different indications. Extract ONLY the age for plaque psoriasis. If the same age applies to all indications, use that.

If age is not explicitly stated in the PA coverage criteria, approval criteria, or authorization requirements section → output "NA".
Sections that do NOT count as age criteria even if they mention age: - "U.S. Food and Drug Administration" informational sections - Background or clinical evidence sections - References sections - FDA indications tables (e.g., a table listing FDA indications per drug) - Clinical trial descriptions
Only explicit age language in the PA decision criteria counts.

CRITICAL: Some documents (e.g., BRM addendums) list many drugs on a single page with inline age annotations next to each drug name: "Stelara (ustekinumab) [≥6 years old]" "Tremfya (guselkumab)" ← no annotation
Extract the age annotation ONLY for {brand}. Do NOT apply another drug's annotation to {brand}. Do NOT assume {brand} shares an adjacent drug's threshold.
If {brand} appears WITHOUT a specific age annotation AND the policy states a general "adult patients" or "adult members" criterion elsewhere: output ">=18". If {brand} appears WITHOUT a specific age annotation AND no general age criterion is found: output "NA".
Example — processing TREMFYA on the document above: - Tremfya has no inline age annotation - General criterion elsewhere says "adult patients" → output ">=18" (NOT ">=6", which belongs to Stelara only)

example.policy_excerpt: Patient meets FDA labeled age for plaque psoriasis.
For members 6 years of age or older for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis.
Adult patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis.
Age is within FDA labeling for the requested indication.
Plaque Psoriasis criteria apply to: - Adult patients (18 years and older) - Pediatric patients (6 years and older)
example.reasoning: Policy has two age groups: >=18 and >=6. Output the youngest: >=6.

example.description: Multi-indication age table — PsO-specific row wins
example.policy_excerpt: Age Restrictions: Individual is 18 years of age or older, except for the diagnosis of JIA and plaque psoriasis. For PsA and JIA, individual is 2 years of age or older. For plaque psoriasis, 4 years of age or older.
example.reasoning: The policy lists different ages per indication. Rule 5 says extract ONLY the plaque psoriasis age. The PsO-specific threshold is explicitly "4 years of age or older". Do NOT use the general threshold (>=18) or the JIA/PsA threshold (>=2). Output >=4.

example.description: Age not mentioned in PA criteria — return NA
example.policy_excerpt: For moderate to severe plaque psoriasis: 1. Diagnosis of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis; AND 2. Trial and failure of at least one conventional systemic therapy (methotrexate, cyclosporine, or acitretin); AND 3. Must be prescribed by a dermatologist.
example.reasoning: No age language appears anywhere in these PA criteria. Do NOT infer or apply any FDA-labeled age from training knowledge. The absence of age criteria means the policy does not restrict by age. Output NA.

example.description: Program-wide FDA labeling deference — BCBS/plan format
example.policy_excerpt: Target Agent(s) will be approved when ALL of the following are met: ... 9. If the patient has an FDA labeled indication, then ONE of the following: A. The patient's age is within FDA labeling for the requested indication for the requested agent OR B. There is support for using the requested agent for the patient's age for the requested indication
example.reasoning: Criterion 9A explicitly defers to FDA labeling for age — this triggers Rule 1. Do NOT look up or apply a specific number from training knowledge. Do NOT treat the "adult patients" FDA indication text as a PA criterion.
